newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LALIME SETS GOALIE RECORD WITH 15TH STRAIGHT UNBEATEN GAME.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LALIME SETS GOALIE RECORD WITH 15TH STRAIGHT UNBEATEN GAME.

text.p: Patrick Lalime turned aside 31 shots and set an NHL record for the best career start by a goalie as the Pittsburgh Penguins defeated the Hartford Whalers, 3-0 to extend their unbeaten streak to 13 games.

With the win, Lalime improved to 13-0-2. The 15-game unbeaten string at the start of a career broke the mark set by Ken Dryden, who went 12-0-2 for the 1970-71 Montreal Canadiens, and Ross Brooks, who went 11-0-3 for the 1972-73 Boston Bruins.
"The teamwork has been important," Lalime said. "Everybody has been playing great in front of me and that has been a big plus."
"I cannot say enough about this kid. He has been amazing," said Penguins coach Eddie Johnston.
In Calgary, Theo Fleury scored with 36 seconds left in the second period to snap a tie and Trevor Kidd turned aside 20 shots as the Calgary Flames edged the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, 2-1.
After Yves Racine scored his first goal of the season midway through the first period to knot the score at 1-1, Fleury gave the Flames a lead they wouldn't relinquish with his 19th marker.

At the Islanders, Matthew Barnaby scored the tie-breaking goal with three minutes left and rookie Steve Shields made 25 saves in his second start of the season as the Buffalo Sabres edged the reeling New York Islanders, 2-1.

With the score tied 1-1, Michal Grosek broke down the left side and into the New York zone. He centred a pass down low into the slot to Barnaby, who circled around goaltender Eric Fichaud before sliding the puck into the left side of the net for his 10th goal of the season.
Donald Audette also scored for the Sabres.

In Ottawa, Ron Tugnutt made 21 saves and just missed his first shutout in over three years and Daniel Alfredsson and Randy Cunneyworth each had a goal and two assists to lift the Ottawa Senators to a 5-1 rout of the Washington Capitals.
Tugnutt had a shutout until Chris Simon beat him with a wrist shot from the inside of the right circle on a 4-on-4 with 6:56 left in the game.
Alexandre Daigle and Alexei Yashin added goals for the Senators.

In Phoenix, Pierre Turgeon had his first two-goal game of the season and added an assist and Grant Fuhr turned aside 24 shots, helping the St. Louis Blues to a 4-1 victory over the slumping Phoenix Coyotes.
Geoff Courtnall and Scott Pellerin also scored for St. Louis, which scored the only three goals of the third period to snap a 1-1 tie.
Pellerin's fourth goal of the season 3:30 into the period gave St. Louis the lead for good.

In Toronto, Kai Nurminen and Ed Olczyk scored 73 seconds apart late in the third period as the Los Angeles Kings rallied to a 3-2 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs, who suffered their sixth straight loss.

Mats Sundin scored at 5:14 of the third period to give the Leafs a 2-1 lead, but Nurminen tallied his second goal of the game and ninth of the season to tie it with 5:02 remaining before Olczyk won it a minute later.
Byron Dafoe had 40 saves for the Kings.
In Edmonton, Curtis Joseph stopped 40 shots for his fifth shutout of the season and Ryan Smyth scored twice on the power play to lead the Edmonton Oilers to a 4-0 victory over the Florida Panthers.
Joseph's best saves came in a flurry with roughly six minutes left in the game. He stopped four shots from close range before the puck was cleared.
Todd Marchant and Daniel McGillis added goals and Jason Arnott assisted on both of Smyth's markers for the Oilers.

In Colorado, Keith Jones scored with 8:30 left and Sandis Ozolinsh added an insurance goal 3:36 later as the Colorado Avalanche tied a team-record 11-game unbeaten streak with a 4-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Aaron Miller had a goal and an assist and Patrick Roy made 27 saves for the Avalanche, who improved to 8-0-3 during the streak and have not lost since December 21st.
Daymond Langkow and Paul Ysebaert scored for the Lightning.
